sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Mallikarjuna Rao
 Criminal Petition No.9485 of 2023

Order:
1.
The Petitioner, arrayed as Accused in Cr.No.175 of 2023 of Avanigadda Police Station, Krishna District, filed this Criminal Petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., seeking anticipatory bail.

2. A case has been registered against the Petitioners for the offence punishable under Section 344,
376(2)(n), 506 of I.P.C.
3.

The Prosecution's case, in brief, is that Defacto Complainant's elder daughter, Dasari Venkata Nancharamma (hereinafter referred to as 'Victim'), studying 1st Degree at SVL College, Avanigadda,
on 04.09.2023, at 12.00 hrs, he asked the Victim why she didn't go to college, for which, she replied that she would go in the afternoon for exams and then subsequently, she left after lunch; at 15.00 hrs, he found out that the Victim left the house by writing a letter; then he searched for her in the surrounding vicinity, but in vain.
Then, the Defacto Complainant complained.
Initially, the Police registered a case U/Sec.174 of Cr.P.C., as 'Woman Missing'; subsequently, it was altered to Sections 344, 376(2)(n), 506 of I.P.C., and the Petitioner, arraigned as Accused.

The investigation reveals that the Victim was kidnapped and raped multiple times at Vellore by the Accused and that, finally,
the Victim escaped from his house at Vellore and went back to her house.
T.M.R., J 4.

The brief averments of the Petitioner's case are that he is falsely implicated in this case with an ulterior motive only to wreak vengeance; in fact, the Victim eloped with the Petitioner voluntarily and cohabited with him for a prolonged period; the ingredients of the alleged offences against the Petitioner are not attracted in any manner; there is an inordinate and unexplained delay and deliberate afterthought in lodging the F.I.R., which is fatal to the Prosecution's case; he is not primarily present in the scene of offences; investigation is almost completed, so, he cannot tamper with the evidence.
5. On the contrary, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed the petition because the investigation was not completed.
If the Petitioner is enlarged on anticipatory bail, there is a possibility of tampering with the evidence.
6. I have heard both sides.
Learned counsel on both sides reiterated their submission on par with the contentions presented in the petition and the report.
Consequently, the arguments raised by learned counsel need not be reproduced.

sentences.text: The Victim, in her report, stated that she frequently spoke with the Accused over the phone, and he spoke to her indecently.
Fearing harm to her family, she went to Chilakaluripeta, and the Accused took her to Vellore town in Tamil Nadu, where he raped her twice.
T.M.R., J 8.
The Petitioner's counsel relies on a letter dated 04.09.2023, written by the Victim, to assert that she left her house willingly with a man of her choice.
In this letter, she expressed her intention to see her parents only after settling in life, citing inevitable circumstances for leaving home.

The Petitioner also submitted a letter to the Station House Officer, emphasizing that the Victim, being about 20 years old, had the right to live with a man of her choice and willingly accompanied him.
Photographs were provided to show that she left the house voluntarily.
However, at this stage, this Court is not inclined to accept the Petitioner's claim based on the letter addressed by the Victim to the Investigating Officer while in the company of the Petitioner.
9. The Victim, aged about 20 years, and the Petitioner, aged about 60 years, have a significant age difference.
Determining whether the Victim's consent was voluntary or based on a misconception of fact lacks a straight jacket formula.
The report lodged by the Victim's father indicates that she was pursuing a degree and engaged in domestic work.
It appears that she trusted the Petitioner and left her house with the intention of settling in life.

Given the age gap and socio-economic background,
characterizing their relationship as a love affair seems implausible.
The Victim's father is also approximately 60 years old, and the Victim, being young and from a low-income family, may not have fully understood the consequences of her actions.
The circumstances and material on record suggest that the Victim went to Vellore seeking a settlement in life with the Petitioner's assistance.
The report by the Victim alleges that the T.M.R., J Petitioner raped her twice against her will.
The overall circumstances do not indicate a strong desire on the part of the Victim to live with the Petitioner; instead, the letter she left suggests a desire to settle down in life.
The question of consent is to be ascertained through a careful examination of all relevant circumstances.
This Court views that an act under the influence of inevitable compulsion does not constitute legal consent, and a threat of force is sufficient.
10. Regarding the Prosecution's case, the investigation remains incomplete.
The anticipatory bail for the Petitioner may adversely impact the ongoing investigation.
There is a possibility of threats to the Victim, and there exists a prima facie case implicating the Petitioner in a serious offence.
The nature of the accusations is grave, involving allegations of rape.
The investigation agency has not had the opportunity to interrogate the Accused/Petitioner.
The Petitioner has not claimed that he cooperated with the investigation agency, and there is a potential risk of absconding.
Custodial interrogation is deemed necessary to extract all material information related to the offence.
In light of the grounds presented in the petition, it is evident that the Petitioner does not contest staying with the Victim in Vellore.

The letter dated 02.10.2023, addressed to the Station House Officer,
Avanigadda Police Station, indicates willful cohabitation between the Petitioner and the Victim.
Prima facie, the material establishes a case under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.

The established legal principle is that anticipatory bail is not granted as a matter of rule; it should only be granted when the Court is convinced that exceptional T.M.R., J circumstances warrant such an Gidivaka Seshagirirao vs The State Of Andhra Rpadesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131293628/
2 extraordinary remedy.

sentences.text: Considering the gravity of the offence and potential punishment in light of the allegations, the Petitioner has not made out a prima facie case for bail under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

11. It is explicitly clarified that the observations made in this order are preliminary and pertain solely to the decision on the present application without indicating a stance on the merits of the case.
12. Given the above facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that it is not desirable to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner/Accused at this stage.
13. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is dismissed.
In this Criminal Petition, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE T. MALLIKARJUNA RAO Dated: 15.12.2023 SAK T.M.R., J THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE T MALLIKARJUNA RAO CRIMINAL PETITION NO. 9485 of 2023 Date: 15.12.2023
